Atlas Lithium is a mineral development company implementing its first mine and processing facility at its 100%-owned Neves Project, our material mineral property.
Our current focus is the continued advancement of the Neves Project, our hard-rock lithium project in the Lithium Valley area of Minas Gerais state in Brazil, toward active mining.

We intend to mine and then process our lithium-containing ore to produce lithium concentrate (also known as spodumene concentrate), a key ingredient for the energy storage system and electric vehicle battery supply chain.

We have disclosed mineral resources and mineral reserves for the Neves Project based on our technical report summary, effective May 15, 2025, as updated on June 16, 2026 (see Exhibit 96.1 to our 2025 Annual Report).
During the third quarter of 2026, we continued to advance our flagship Neves Project toward production while achieving several important milestones.
On July 13, 2026, we announced that the Neves Project remains on track toward first commercial production of lithium oxide concentrate, which would mark our transition from developer to producer.

The Neves Project, which is 100%-owned by us and fully permitted through commercial production, will feature a vertically integrated mining and processing industrial complex designed to produce approximately 146,000 tonnes of lithium concentrate per year, as detailed in our definitive feasibility study (the “DFS”).

On September 9, 2026, we announced the execution of contracts and firm agreements covering key aspects of project implementation, including engineering, earthworks and civil construction, electromechanical assembly, electrical infrastructure, construction management, and logistics.
We believe that securing such contracts at or below DFS estimates reduces project execution and cost risks.
We anticipate that the fully integrated Neves Project facility will generate a large and positive economic impact in the Jequitinhonha Valley, a developing region of Minas Gerais state in Brazil.
Our current full-time employees at Neves Project already earn, on average, twice the prevailing local wage and receive healthcare coverage and other benefits that exceed regional standards.

While the lithium market remains subject to price volatility and evolving supply and demand dynamics, we believe that our anticipated position among the lowest-cost lithium producers should provide meaningful margin protection across a range of pricing environments.

If the needed financing is not available, or if the terms of financing are less desirable than we expect, we may be forced to scale back our existing operations and growth plans, which could have an adverse impact on our business and financial prospects and could raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
Dollar is the primary currency through which we and our Brazilian subsidiaries expect to raise any additional capital.
